text:
maria: Heads up — aggregate counts for clicks/hour show a gap for 2025-10-04 02:00-05:00 UTC. Looks like late ingestion hit the kafka cluster and a few windows never materialized. Thinking we should run a targeted recompute/backfill. Need to decide routing (dedicated vs shared), rate/quota plan, and console UX (dry-run, concurrency). Any objections?
chetan: Agree we need a recompute, but cardinality is non-trivial — ~1.2B events over the 3h window across ~200 logical shards. If we run naive full recompute it'll impact hosted SLOs.
samir: We should do slice-level incremental rehydrate first (only affected partitions). Also throttle replay via a token-bucket on replay-worker. Proposed rate config:
```json
{
  "mode": "slice-incremental",
  "concurrency": 4,
  "rate_per_worker": 5000,
  "dedupe_window_ms": 600000
}
```
lisa: From Console side: add a "Start Backfill" modal with options: [slice-only, full, dry-run], a concurrency slider, and a checkbox for "route to dedicated-backfill pool". Default to slice-only + dry-run. Show estimated infra impact before confirming.
maria: Good. We should also expose an internal API: `POST /v1/telemetry/recompute-run` that accepts `{mode, shard_filter, concurrency, priority}` and returns a `recompute_run_id`. Console + CLI will use it.
dmitri: Important: dedupe is expensive if we re-ingest into the same aggregates table. We must ensure idempotent upserts. Suggest we write recompute outputs to `recompute_results` with `recompute_run_id` and then MERGE into `aggregates` using `max(event_offset)` / last_seen logic.
chetan: :thumbsup: Also propose tagging runs with `priority=low` and a routing policy that sends them to `dedicated-backfill` pool. If pool not available fallback to `throttled-hosted` lane. That will protect customers.
replay-bot: job 0x9f3e started by maria: mode=slice-incremental slices=2025-10-04T02..05 concurrency=4 rate=5000r/s
samir: Quick dry-run on one slice: estimate ~12m runtime, peak mem 42GB, cpu 6 cores. So concurrency=4 -> roughly 168GB across workers. Staging can absorb that, prod cluster is tight unless we route to dedicated pool.
lisa: UX note: add a warning banner in modal: "Expected infra impact: ~12m per slice, ~42GB memory per worker. Recommend dedicated-backfill for prod." Also show an option to schedule during off-peak.
maria: Decision for canary: implement API + console modal, and canary the flow to eng-sre and a small set of telemetry-runbook owners on Thursday 03:00 UTC. We'll add a routing policy that prefers `dedicated-backfill` and caps total tokens/throughput.
dmitri: I'll implement idempotency via `recompute_run_id` and store a `merge_manifest` table so we can reconcile results and rollback if necessary. Will also add `recompute_run_id` to metric tags.
chetan: Let's also emit metrics: `recompute.run.duration`, `recompute.run.tokens_processed`, `recompute.run.estimated_memory`, `recompute.impact.customers_throttled`. Expose them in Console under "Backfills" dashboard so SRE can watch.
ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: canary deploy for recompute-api on 2025-10-09 03:00 UTC — pinging #eng-sre for blast radius sign-off
maria: I'll open the API PR and sketch the console mock today. SQL merge sketch for the dedupe approach I'm attaching here:
```sql
WITH computed AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, hour, SUM(clicks) AS clicks, MAX(event_offset) AS max_offset
  FROM recompute_results
  WHERE recompute_run_id = :run
  GROUP BY tenant_id, hour
)
MERGE INTO aggregates a
USING computed c
ON a.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND a.hour = c.hour
WHEN MATCHED AND c.max_offset > a.last_offset THEN
  UPDATE SET clicks = c.clicks, last_offset = c.max_offset
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
  INSERT (tenant_id, hour, clicks, last_offset) VALUES (c.tenant_id, c.hour, c.clicks, c.max_offset);
```
maria: Thanks all — followups: @lisa please post console mock in Figma, @dmitri add merge_manifest schema, @samir run a batch of dry-runs across 10 slices and paste numbers here, @chetan prepare routing policy PR. We'll reconvene after dry-run numbers come in.
